subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation — GPU portfolio, quantization, and throughput packing

Subject: RFI: GPU portfolio & quantization — Acme reservation questionnaire

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for meeting last week. As part of our procurement packet we need a concise RFI response focused on dedicated reservation sizing. Our priorities are predictable throughput for two production models (chat-12B encoder-decoder, and embed-3B), cost-sensitive inference (target $/1M tokens), and a fallback plan if reserved capacity is stressed.

Can you provide:
- recommended GPU SKUs (performance and cost tradeoffs),
- measured tokens/sec or QPS per SKU for both models (95th/99th tail latency),
- suggested reservation mix (committed pool sizing + burst),
- quantization profiles you support and any throughput delta,
- examples of how Redwood routes/falls back when a SKU is unavailable.

We'd like a short workbook and any benchmark PDFs by EOD Aug 30 to attach to our internal vendor evaluation.

Thanks,
Tim
Procurement, Acme Health

Subject: Re: RFI: GPU portfolio & quantization — Acme reservation questionnaire (Redwood response)

Hi Tim / Lori — thank you for the clear ask. Attached are the workbook and bench report; below is a concise Q&A and the recommended reservation packing strategy. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min review to walk the workbook line-by-line.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Recommended SKUs: A100-80GB (FP16 primary), A100-40GB (cost-balanced), H100-80GB for low-latency/throughput-critical slices. We also support T4/RTX6000 for small embed-only pools.
- Quantization: INT8 (our supported post-training quant) typically yields 1.7–2.2x throughput vs FP16 on A100/H100 depending on model ops. For embed-3B we see ~2.0x token throughput with INT8 and minimal quality delta in our evals.
- Throughput (representative bench; see attached pdf for full vectors):
  - chat-12B (FP16): A100-80GB — 420 tokens/sec (sustained), p95=86ms, p99=190ms. A100-80GB (INT8): 920 tokens/sec, p95=92ms, p99=220ms (note: higher throughput increases tail variance). H100-80GB (FP16): 560 tokens/sec, p95=70ms, p99=160ms.
  - embed-3B (FP16): A100-40GB — 3,600 embeddings/sec, INT8: 7,200 embeddings/sec. T4 (FP16): 1,100 embeddings/sec (cost-efficient but higher latency variance).
- Reservation mix recommendation (by usage bucket):
  - Pilot (25K tokens/min sustained): 1x A100-40GB dedicated slot + 1 small shared burst lane (T4)
  - Growth (500K tokens/min sustained): 3 A100-80GB reserved + 1 H100-80GB on hot-pool; burst capacity equivalent to 2 A100-80GB
  - Production (4M tokens/min sustained): 10 A100-80GB reserved + 4 H100-80GB reserved (for low-latency endpoints) + 6 A100-40GB reserve for background batch/embeddings. Configure an autoscale burst pool with capacity to absorb +30% sustained spikes.
- Cost assumptions: workbook includes per-hour MSRP and Redwood committed discount tiers; expected $/1M tokens varies by SKU and quant profile — INT8 on A100 reduces unit cost ~45% vs FP16 for throughput-bound workloads.
- Tail-latency and SLA: design reservation pools with a mix of H100 capacity for latency-critical routes (p99 targets) and A100 for cost-efficient throughput. Use request-level priority tagging and token-preserving prefix cache to lower p99 on common prefixes.

Fallback and routing behavior (how Redwood keeps you online):
- Smart routing: primary route to customer reserved pool (zone/region). If reserved pool reaches 85% utilization we open burst lanes from a configurable burst pool (dedicated hot-pool or shared).
- Graceful degradation: priority=high requests rerouted to H100 or smaller context-preserving models; non-critical requests are queued to batch on cheaper A100-40GB instances (with increased response time).
- Model variants: we support model families that are compatible for graceful fallback (e.g., chat-12B -> chat-12B-quantized or chat-8B for extreme degradation). Routing respects semantic compatibility rules supplied in the workbook.

Quantization profiles and caveats:
- Supported flows: FP16 (baseline), INT8 post-training quant (recommended for embed-3B and for chat-12B where eval shows acceptable deltas), mixed precision for memory-constrained SKUs.
- Operational guidance: validate on your eval prompts (we include an eval harness in the workbook) — INT8 can introduce occasional hallucination shifts; we recommend a canary with 5–10% traffic before wide rollout.

Reservation packing strategy (how we pack different workloads to GPUs):
- Pack embeddings and short-context chat on A100-40GB into higher-density bins; reserve larger contexts & latency-sensitive endpoints on H100/A100-80GB.
- Use continuous batching for embeddings with a high max-batch window (configurable) to increase tokens/sec while respecting p95 SLO.
- Slotting guide (workbook table): preferred mix by % workload for Production: 55% A100-80GB (throughput), 20% H100 (latency-critical), 25% A100-40GB (embeddings & batch).

Acceptance testing and benchmarks provided:
- Throughput-benchmarks-rt-20260828.pdf — includes raw bench logs, p50/p95/p99, and CPU/GPU utilization curves.
- Redwood-reservation-workbook-acme-v1.xlsx — scenario tabs (Pilot/Growth/Production), cost math, slotting worksheet, rollout checklist.
- Fallback-playbook-acme.docx — step-by-step operational runbook for overflow events and cross-region failover.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Acme prefers H100-first for latency-critical customers (we can show cost delta).
2) We can run a 24-48 hour dedicated bench on a snapshot of your eval prompts if you provide 500 representative queries (we'll sign an NDA if needed).
3) Schedule 30-min walkthrough — available Thu/Fri next week.

Thanks — happy to refine.

Best,
